questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The road __has been rough__, they abandoned their journey further.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'being rough'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence needs a correct participial phrase to indicate the reason or condition.
 
• "Being rough" correctly functions as a participial phrase explaining why they abandoned their journey.
 
• It provides a direct cause-and-effect relationship: the condition of the road (being rough) caused them to abandon their journey.
 
• The use of "being" appropriately conveys continuous action at the time they made their decision.
 
• "Being rough" fits seamlessly into the sentence structure to describe the ongoing state of the road.
 
• This option maintains the semantic flow, ensuring that the sentence is grammatically correct and logically sound.

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 "be rough" is incorrect because it is in the base form and does not fit the sentence grammatically or contextually.
 
• Option 2 "was rough" is not a suitable substitution because it leads to a comma splice if not restructured.
 
• Option 3 "had been rough" is incorrect because it implies a state before another past state, which complicates the timeline unnecessarily.

questions.solution:

__
 
• In the given sentence, the use of the preposition **'beside'** in the underlined segment is incorrect.
 
• It implies something happening unrelated to the project.
 
• **"In the project"** suggests the unexpected turn occurred within the project itself.
 
 
• **Example:** *I will be with you **in** a moment.*
 
 
 
• Hence, **"in the project"** is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

**Complete Sentence: **The unexpected turn **in the project__ **put the company in a big financial crisis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The rest of the options are incorrect because:
 
 
• **'until the project': **This phrase focuses on timing and implies the crisis happened sometime before the project's completion.
 
• **'between the project':** This suggests something happening in the space between different project stages.

questions.question:
Directions: Select the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the word given in the sentence:

I know you don't like her, but do you have to make it so **__obvious__**?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**obscure**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Obvious** refers to something that is easily perceived, understood, or recognized and that requires little thought or effort to see or comprehend. It implies a level of clearness and visibility, and suggests that something is plain, self-evident or patent. (स्पष्ट का तात्पर्य किसी ऐसी चीज से है जिसे आसानी से समझा या पहचाना जा सकता है और जिसे देखने या समझने के लिए बहुत कम विचार या प्रयास की आवश्यकता होती है। इसका तात्पर्य स्पष्टता और दृश्यता के स्तर से है, और यह सुझाव देता है कि कुछ सादा, स्वतः स्पष्ट या पेटेंट है।) 

 
 
• **Example***: An **obvious** solution, which is easy to see and understand.*
 
 
 
• **Obscure** can refer to something that is unclear, difficult to understand, or unknown. ("अस्पष्ट" किसी ऐसी चीज़ को संदर्भित कर सकता है जो अस्पष्ट, समझने में कठिन या अज्ञात है।)​
 
 
• **Example**: *The meaning of the poem was so **obscure** that even the literary experts had trouble deciphering it.*
 
 
 
• From the above points, it is clear that Obvious and Obscure are antonyms of each other.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option no.1"**​

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

**Let's see the meanings of the other given words:**

__
 
• **Tangible**: A tangible object is something that can be touched or felt physically. (एक ऐसी चीज है जिसे भौतिक रूप से छुआ या महसूस किया जा सकता है। उदाहरण के लिए, एक किताब, फर्नीचर का एक टुकड़ा, या कपड़ों का एक टुकड़ा सभी मूर्त वस्तुएँ हैं।)

 
 
• **For example,** *a book, a piece of furniture, or a piece of clothing are all **tangible** objects. *
 
 
 
• **Apparent**: Something that is apparent is clearly visible or evident to the senses or the mind. (कुछ जो स्पष्ट है वह स्पष्ट रूप से दिखाई देता है या इंद्रियों या मन के लिए स्पष्ट है। उदाहरण के लिए, यदि किसी को बुखार है और उसे बहुत अधिक पसीना आ रहा है, तो यह स्पष्ट है कि वह अस्वस्थ है।)
 
 
• **For example,** *if someone has a fever and is sweating profusely, it's **apparent** that they are unwell. *
 
 
 
• **Certain**: When you say that you are certain about something, you mean that you are confident or sure that it's true. (जब आप कहते हैं कि आप किसी चीज़ के बारे में निश्चित हैं, तो आपका मतलब है कि आप आश्वस्त हैं या सुनिश्चित हैं कि यह सच है।)
 
 
• For example, * I am **certain** that I locked the door before leaving the house.*

questions.question:
**Directions:** item in this section consists of a sentence with an underlined word followed by four words. Select the option that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word and mark your response in your Answer Sheet accordingly.

A trip to the hills was __refreshing__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**wearying**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Refreshing **refers to something that is invigorating, rejuvenating, or provides a sense of renewed energy. (ताजगी भरा)

 
 
• **Example**: A **refreshing **walk in the morning can set a positive tone for the day.
 
 
 
• The opposite of refreshing is something that causes fatigue or exhaustion, which fits the definition of the word '**wearying**'. (थकाऊ)
 
 
• **Example**: Long hours of studying can be **wearying **for students and may lead to decreased productivity.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct antonym is '**wearying**'.

Therefore, the correct answer is “**Option 2**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conniving **(षड्यंत्रकारी): This term is not related to the term 'refreshing'. It refers to secretly cooperating or plotting, typically for malicious purposes.
 
• **Revivifying **(पुनर्जीवित करना): This serves as a synonym for 'refreshing', not an antonym. It means to give new life or vigor to.
 
• **Rejuvenating **(नवजीवन देनेवाला): This is another synonym for 'refreshing'. It means to make someone or something look or feel better, younger, or more vital.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

As technology evolves, consumers increasingly _______________ products with enhanced features and greater efficiency.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**demand**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The context tells us that with technological advancement, customers are progressively seeking products offering improved features and higher efficiency.
 
• The verb "**demand**" is the **base form of the verb**, which is appropriate here because the sentence describes a general trend or habit.
 
• **"Demand"** is **plural **here (referring to consumers), so the verb form is **"demand."** The plural noun **"consumers"** correctly aligns with the plural verb **"demand,"** making it grammatically accurate.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"As technology evolves, consumers increasingly **demand**__ products with enhanced features and greater efficiency."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "might demand"** indicates a possibility rather than a trend, making it less suitable for this sentence.
 
• **Option 3: "has demanded"** suggests a completed action, which does not fit the ongoing nature of the trend described.
 
• **Option 4: "were demanding"** is in the past continuous tense, which does not match the context of an evolving trend.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

If we wish to _______ a democratic country, we must __________ to our constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank in the sentence needs to be filled with words that convey maintaining a democratic country and following the constitution.
 
• The word "**remain**" signifies continuing in a particular state, and "**adhere**" means to stick firmly to a rule or principle.
 
• These words fit perfectly in the context of maintaining democracy and following the constitution.
 
• The other options do not convey the meaning as effectively or are grammatically incorrect.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *If we wish to remain__ a democratic country, we must __adhere__ to our constitution.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Govern**: means to rule or manage, but it does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Fasten**: means to attach or secure, which is unrelated to the context.
 
• **Uphold**: means to maintain or support, but its pair "lead" does not align with the sentence.
 
• **Hold**: means to maintain or grasp, but it does not fit grammatically or contextually here.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with appropriate modal verb :

When I was a boy, I ___________ walk forty miles in a day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**could'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In this context, "**could**" is the correct choice because it is used to express ability or possibility in the past, which is the purpose of this sentence.
 
• It indicates that the speaker had the ability to walk forty miles in a day when he was a boy.
 
• Let's break down the options:
 
 
• "**should**" - This modal verb is used to express obligation, advice, expectation, or speculation. It does not denote ability or possibility, which is required in this context.
 
• "**can**" - This modal verb is used to express present ability or possibility, not past ability or possibility, which is the focus of this sentence.
 
• "**could**" - This is the correct choice. It's often used to express an ability or possibility in the past, which fits the context of this sentence. In this case, "could" suggests that when the speaker was a boy, he had the ability to walk forty miles in a day.
 
• "**must**" - This modal verb is used to express obligation, necessity, or strong certainty. It does not express past ability or possibility, which is required in this context.
